items.text: People should be allowed to use private messaging that only the sender and receiver can ever read, even under a court order.
items.rationale: Strong privacy position (no lawful-access exception); cypherpunks, libertarians, civil libertarians. Clarified 'allowed' (legal permission, not provision).

items.text: Police should need a judge's permission before searching someone's home or phone, even if this lets some guilty people go free.
items.rationale: Concrete anchor replaces status-quo-relative 'strict limits'; cost clause stops it being consensus. Loose mirror of lib-09.

items.text: If a serious emergency is declared, public protests should be allowed to go ahead.
items.rationale: Hard conditional (condition favours Security). Toned down from 'fully protected' to match level 2. Touches emergency-powers gap; disclose.

items.text: Law-abiding adults should be allowed to own a gun for self-defence.
items.rationale: Adds a right-coded Liberty item (review: poles leaned left/right). Strong frame-split candidate across countries. May cross-load on pro.

items.text: If officials are found misusing a surveillance power, that power should be abolished rather than reformed.
items.note: Surveillance power = a legal power to monitor people, such as phone tapping or location tracking.
items.rationale: Easy conditional (favours Liberty); 'abolished rather than reformed' removes the ambiguity of 'taken away entirely'. Frame split via trust in today's officials.

items.text: Speech that stirs up hatred against people because of their race, religion or similar traits should be a crime.
items.rationale: Left/communitarian-coded Security item; narrowed from 'a group of people' so supporters recognise it.

items.text: Public places should have cameras that automatically identify people, so wanted criminals and missing people can be found quickly.
items.rationale: Universal ID surveillance in public; purpose added so it is not a strawman. Frame split: trusted ideal rulers vs today's.

items.text: If a deadly epidemic is spreading, people should be required to stay home when health authorities say so.
items.rationale: Easy conditional (favours Security); left/public-health-coded Security item. Touches emergency-powers gap; disclose.

items.text: Police should be able to stop and search people they find suspicious, even if many innocent people get searched.
items.rationale: Concrete version replaces status-quo-relative 'wide powers'; cost clause keeps it polar. Loose mirror of lib-02.

items.text: If a drug mainly harms only the people who use it, possessing it should be a crime.
items.rationale: Hard conditional (condition favours Liberty): strong paternalist enforcement. Criminal enforcement belongs on lib per spec; cross-loads on pro, disclose.

items.text: If a party aims to abolish free elections, it should be barred from running in them.
items.rationale: Militant democracy / paradox of tolerance (review B4, P1). Restricting who may contest is the Security pole. Mirrors lib-12's condition style. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.

items.text: If a political system blocks needed change, overthrowing it by force can be right.
items.rationale: Method of change (review C5): the right of revolution against an order, the Liberty pole. Splits revolutionary from reformist socialists, mainly in the here-and-now frame. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.
